Welcome. I’m really glad you’re here, because together, we’re about to step into a world where the line between sanity and madness isn’t as sharp as you might think. Have you ever wondered what it truly means to be “sane”—or felt that sense of being split, somehow both present and absent in your own life?
That’s exactly the kind of experience we’ll explore as we journey through the insights of R.D. Laing, woven into his thought-provoking book, The Divided Self: An Existential Study in Sanity and Madness. Laing invites us to look deeper—beyond labels and surface judgments—to really feel what it's like when someone becomes a stranger to themselves, searching for connection while fighting an internal battle that’s as real as any physical struggle.
What happens when the sense of self starts to crack under pressure? How do ordinary moments unravel into confusion and isolation? Laing’s work gently asks us to set aside assumptions about mental illness and, instead, witness the vulnerability and courage at the heart of the human experience.
So, as we move forward, let’s open ourselves to new ways of understanding—ways that bring a little more empathy, a little more curiosity, and perhaps even hope for healing. Ready to walk this path together? Let’s begin.
